B) Greek
C) Hungarian
D) Norwegian
E) Turkish
raw_logic_programs:

days = EnumSort([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
languages = EnumSort([French, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Norwegian, Turkish])
film = Function([days] -> [languages])

# Constraints
Distinct([d:days], film(d)) ::: exactly six different films will be shown, one each day
Count([d:days], film(d) == Norwegian) == 2 ::: two films in Norwegian available
Count([d:days], film(d) == Italian) == 2 ::: two films in Italian available
Count([d:days], film(d) == Greek) == 2 ::: two films in Greek available
Count([d:days], film(d) == French) == 2 ::: two films in French available
Count([d:days], film(d) == Hungarian) == 2 ::: two films in Hungarian available

B) There is exactly one digit between the digit 1 and the digit 2.
C) There are at most two digits between the digit 1 and the digit 3.
D) There are at most two digits between the digit 2 and the digit 3.
E) There are at most two digits between the digit 2 and the digit 4.

positions = EnumSort([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
code = Function([positions] -> [digits])

# Constraints

code(2) == 2 * code(1) ::: The second digit has a value exactly twice that of the first digit
code(3) < code(5) ::: The value of the third digit is less than the value of the fifth digit

# Options
Question ::: Which one of the following must be true about any acceptable product code?

is_valid(ForAll([code:code], Count([p:positions], And(p != position_of(2), p != position_of(4), And(position_of(2) < p, p < position_of(4)) Or And(position_of(4) < p, p < position_of(2)))) <= 2)) ::: (E)
